documentNotes.title: Instructions
documentNotes.statement:
1. During observation test using small telescope, you will receive :

- Problem sheet
- Answer sheet
- Additional sheet
- Flashlight

2. During naked eye test, you will receive :

- Problem sheet
- Answer sheet
- Additional sheet
- Flashlight

3. During observation test using main telescope, you will receive :

- Problem sheet
- Answer sheet
- Additional sheet
- Headlamp
- Clip Board

4. During observation test using planetarium (in case of rainy or cloudy), you will receive :

- Problem sheet
- Answer sheet
- Additional sheet
- Flashlight
- Clip Board

5. Please write your student ID in every answer sheet :

6. The total duration for naked eye + small telescope observation is 60 minutes, main telescope 20 minutes, planetarium 15 minutes

paper.caveat: The six numbered tasks share one answer chart and are preserved as one complete observing exercise. The printed task points total 100, but no overall total is printed. The 60-minute duration in the general instructions is shared by naked-eye and small-telescope observations. The Messier table prints M20 twice with different data, and the answer maps print Nova Sagitarii; both are retained. The official key numbers the five brightest stellar positions but supplies no explicit list of their names. For part 6 it gives angular tolerances only, without a numerical Nunki–Shaula separation.

sections.statement:
In the blank square given in the answer sheet, you should assume that Nova Sagittarii 2 is in the center. (marked by green star)

RA(J2000) : 18h 36m 56.84s

Dec(J2000) : -28$^{\circ}$ 55’ 39.8”

Draw Declination and Right Ascension lines passing through Nova Sagittarii. Also draw parallel gridlines at convenient interval and label the accordingly. (The field of view is 45$^{\circ}$)
Mark with filled circle, the five brightest stars in the field of view on the answer sheet along with their names. You can add several other stars for your orientation.
Draw an unfilled circle representing the Moon’s position tomorrow night (on 29 July 2015).
Mark the position of any five Messier Objects in the field of view by cross (x), and write down their names beside their marks.
Draw a line representing the galactic plane.

Mark the positions of Nunki ($\sigma$ Sgr) and Shaula ($\lambda$ Sco) by star (*). Draw a line connecting the two stars. Estimate the angular distance between these stars and write it on the line connecting both stars.
